symptom: A new chat could know recent Powerhouse context and completion/delivery rules yet still ask for redundant approval such as 'if this v2 design is approved', proving that context availability was being mistaken for active runtime governance.
rootCause: Powerhouse had strong preflight, continuity and universal completion contracts, but no mandatory per-run startup receipt that cryptographically bound a specific chat/agent run to the actual canonical preflight/current-state/authority snapshot. Native chat context could therefore influence reasoning without proving that the Powerhouse runtime contract was active.
failedApproach: Treat memory, prior conversation context or policy awareness as sufficient evidence that a new chat is governed, and rely on agent discipline not to repeat approval questions.
fix: Introduce POWERHOUSE-SESSION-BINDING-v1 with a fail-closed session gateway, canonical preflight receipt, authority resolver, no-repeat-approval gate, Agent Fabric completion enforcement and Universal Completion receipt enforcement. Context-only sessions are explicitly POWERHOUSE_UNBOUND.
preventionRule: No material Powerhouse execution or terminal claim may rely on context alone. Bind the run to a verified POWERHOUSE-PREFLIGHT-RECEIPT-v1 first. Before asking the user for approval, resolve canonical authority; if existing authority covers the decision, continue autonomously and block the approval request.
evidence: 2026-09-17 user screenshot: new chat referenced current Powerhouse completion/delivery state but still asked whether a v2 design was approved before implementation.
Repository inspection showed mandatory preflight and universal completion existed but no per-run startup receipt/authority binding contract existed.
open_obligation: Run protected exact-head gates, merge the candidate, read back policy/runtime/preflight/completion integration from main, then update this learning to LIVE_AND_PROVEN with open_obligation null.
